entries.not_relevant_because: Both manuscripts prove Donovan's finiteness: for a bound on defect-group order, blocks of finite groups fall into finitely many Morita equivalence classes, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p ("Donovan's Conjecture over Algebraically Closed Fields") and over W(F̄ₚ) and fixed complete DVRs ("Integral Donovan Finiteness over Witt Vectors"). Neither states or proves a counting identity between the irreducible characters of blocks of G and those of blocks of local subgroups, and neither mentions Dade's conjecture. The character-theoretic inputs they use (the Brauer–Feit bound on simple modules, Cartan entries, cones of projective characters) serve Cartan and Morita bounds, not a Dade-type identity.
